title: Fitbit Alta HR resting heart rate trend leading to early diagnosis and treatment of large vessel vasculitis
summary: Fitbit Alta HR resting-heart-rate rise from 55 to 75 bpm led to early diagnosis and treatment of large vessel vasculitis (Zurich).
account: In a case report published in BMJ Case Reports on 28 February 2022 (event dates not stated; publication date used), a 57-year-old woman in Zurich, Switzerland, noticed in her Fitbit Alta HR application that her resting heart rate had risen persistently from about 55 to about 75 beats per minute over three months, alongside non-specific constitutional symptoms. The elevated resting heart rate led her to seek medical advice at University Hospital Zurich. FDG-PET/CT showed inflammation of the aorta and both subclavian and axillary arteries, consistent with large vessel vasculitis. Treatment with prednisone 50 mg daily and tocilizumab produced rapid improvement; her resting heart rate returned to normal within 10 days and inflammatory markers normalized within two weeks.
purpose: The Fitbit Alta HR computes resting heart rate for fitness tracking; it was not built to detect vasculitis, so this benefit was not its purpose.
system: Fitbit Alta HR resting heart rate (Fitbit app)

ratings.reason: One woman obtained an earlier diagnosis of giant cell arteritis with large vessel involvement and prompt immunosuppressive treatment that resolved her symptoms; a material benefit to one person.

ai_role.statement: The device's resting-heart-rate algorithm produced the trend the patient noticed; there was no alert, and the patient and clinicians drew the inference. The authors credit the elevated resting heart rate with an earlier diagnosis.
